title: Latency Sentry: POP prioritizer using p50/p95 and link-integrity cohort scores
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: We need a region/pop prioritization component (Latency Sentry) that combines p50/p95 latency telemetry with a separate link-integrity (packet loss & error rate) cohort score to produce a single routing rank for POP selection and tiered fallbacks. This ticket covers the scoring algorithm, runtime integration, config knobs for cost-weighted penalties, and a conservative rollout plan. Goal: reduce user-facing tail latency from degraded POPs while minimizing cross-POP egress costs and avoiding oscillation during transient network events.
acceptance_criteria: Latency Sentry produces a stable rank for each POP every 30s window using p50 and p95 plus link-integrity cohort score
Routing decisions reduce p95 for routed requests by >=10% in synthetic degradation experiments without increasing overall token cost by >7%
Hysteresis and cooldown prevent >3 switches/min for a single customer route under realistic traffic patterns
Observability: dashboard showing per-POP composite score, inputs (p50/p95/packet-loss), routing outcomes, and rollback triggers
Integration tests and canary rollout plan validated in dedicated staging and 2 customer-sim clusters
design_decisions: Composite score will weight p95 higher than p50 (default weight 0.7 p95 / 0.3 p50) to prioritize tail latency issues
Link-integrity cohort score (0..1) derived from recent packet loss, TCP retransmit spikes and error-rate; applied as multiplicative penalty to latency score
Use robust percentile estimation with a sliding 3-minute window and exponential smoothing (alpha configurable) to reduce noise
Introduce a cost-penalty term: POPs in different regions incur egress cost factor that can bump their score when near-equal latencies
Hysteresis implemented as threshold + cooldown: change only if new POP score improves current by X% for Y consecutive windows
Model-variant compatibility matrix maintained for fallbacks; only route to POPs that host compatible model variants or mapped compatible quantized variant
implementation_notes: New scoring service to run as part of routing-allocator alongside the existing region-decider; lightweight (Rust) microservice with GRPC interface
Telemetry ingestion: reuse metrics-fanout pipeline (prometheus/push) to compute per-POP percentiles and packet metrics; add pre-aggregated histograms per POP per route-key
Store recent scores in Redis with TTL equal to smoothing window; expose read-only snapshot endpoint for Console
Expose config flags: p95_weight, smoothing_alpha, change_threshold_pct, cooldown_seconds, egress_cost_weight
Fallbacks: when preferred POP lacks compatible model variant, consult variant-mapping service (ENG-96011) and apply variant-degradation-score before routing
Backwards compatibility: default behavior for existing customers remains unchanged until config enabled at tenant-level
testing_plan: Unit tests for percentile estimator and cohort score computation
Integration tests simulating POP degradation (increased latency / packet loss) and asserting routing shift behavior
Chaos runbook: inject transient packet loss spikes and ensure cooldown prevents oscillation
Synthetic load tests to measure cost delta and p95 improvement under multiple traffic mixes
End-to-end staging run against two canary customers and one internal traffic group
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind tenant-level opt-in; enable on internal staging first
Week 1: enable for internal e2e cluster (0% customer traffic) and validate dashboards and alerts
Week 2: enable for 1 low-impact customer with monitoring + on-call watch; run controlled degradation tests
Week 3: enable for 3 mid-tier customers and start slow ramp (10% traffic by routing score) with automated rollback if alert triggers
Full rollout tied to runtime-1.21 release after 2 weeks of stable metrics
